content: If you were required to prioritize three topics in assistive technology for research, which ones would you choose? Do you have any additional comments or suggestions? Would you like to participate in the GATE Research Group meeting? a. No b. Yes: Please provide your name, organization, and email address. Appendix 3 lists the organizations that responded to the questionnaire: 1. AGE-WELL NCE Inc., Canada 2. Australian Rehabilitation & Assistive Technology Association (ARATA) 3. Dong-Eui University, Republic of Korea 4. Elsaesser Consulting Inc., USA 5. European Disability Forum (EDF), Belgium 6. Lund University, Sweden 7. Physical and Rehabilitation Medicine Department, School of Medicine, University of São Paulo, Brazil 8. R2D2 (Rehabilitation Research Design & Disability) Center, USA 9. Raising the Floor International (RtF) 10. Rehabilitation Engineering and Assistive Technology Society of Korea (RESKO) 11. Rehabilitation Engineering Society of North America (RESNA) 12. SINTEF, Norway 13. The Centre of Expertise of Innovative Care and Technology (EIZT), Netherlands 14. Trace R&D Center, USA 15. University of Colorado, Department of Bioengineering, USA 16. University of Pittsburgh, USA 17. University of São Paulo, Brazil 18. University of Wisconsin-Madison, USA 19. University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee, USA A structured discussion was held at the Budapest Congress Centre (Jagello u. 1–3), Liszt Room. The discussion involved four selected topics, conducted in small groups, with each topic discussed for 30 minutes, followed by a 5-minute transition period. The topics discussed were: 1. What are the critical research questions regarding the identification of facilitators and barriers, including cultural and contextual factors, that affect the use of assistive products and services? 2. What are the critical research questions regarding the development of successful models for the delivery, implementation, and support of assistive products and services, including the human resources required? 3. What are the critical research questions regarding how assistive technology products and services, as well as their delivery systems, should be monitored and evaluated? 4. What are the critical research questions regarding policy development to promote the provision of assistive technology products and services, including the role of different stakeholder groups? The meeting concluded with acknowledgments. The core group, consisting of Raymond Grott, Evert-Jan Hoogerwerf, Malcolm MacLachlan, Lisanne Teunissen, and Luc de Witte, drafted this brief with additional contributions from Johan Borg. Four members of the core group represented AAATE or RESNA, the largest professional assistive technology organizations in Europe and North America, respectively, in the absence of equivalent organizations on other continents. Malcolm MacLachlan also participated as the coordinator of the GATE Community Research and Innovation Group. The authors declared no competing interests. The World Health Organization (WHO) expressed gratitude to over 100 experts who contributed to the development of the Global Assistive Technology Priority Research Agenda. This included respondents to the online questionnaire, participants in the research meeting, and peer reviewers. WHO could not acknowledge individual contributions due to the anonymity guaranteed to all questionnaire respondents and meeting participants. The process was jointly coordinated by the following organizations: Advancement of Assistive Technology in Europe (AAATE) Rehabilitation Engineering and Assistive Technology Society of North America (RESNA) Trinity College Dublin, Ireland Zuyd University of Applied Science, Netherlands Financial support was provided by the US Agency for International Development. Design and layout were managed by Inis Communication. The initiative, titled Equipping, Enabling, and Empowering, aims to improve access to assistive technology for everyone, everywhere.
